$comment: Conformance corpus for the RegistryKey grammar (registry-kernel ticket 05). Data, not PHP, so the TS port (ticket 16) and the enum codegen (ticket 12) assert against the SAME cases rather than a re-reading of the prose. Every entry here is executable: tests/Unit/Registries/KeyTest.php drives the first three sections and tests/Unit/Registries/RegistryIndexTest.php drives `routing`. Ticket 30 widened the segment charset to admit `-`, `_` and `:` as internal joiners; the two cases ticket 05 pinned as illegal (`beam_realm`, `beam:realm`) are now legal SINGLE segments, and the joiner-may-not-lead-trail-or-double rule is pinned in their place. Ticket 16 added `routing` — chartered to 21, which closed without it — because longest-prefix routing is the ONLY piece of pure behaviour a second runtime has to reproduce: the grammar ports to a regex and a split, the enums are data, but the walk is an algorithm, and it was the one thing the corpus did not cover. Note for a porter: `Key::SEGMENT_PATTERN` ends in `\z`, which JavaScript does not have — port it as `$`, or the matcher inverts silently.

routing.$comment: Longest-prefix routing over declared roots: which registry owns a key. `roots` are the roots described into the index BESIDE its own; the index always declares the zero-segment root, so a case never lists it. `owner` is the root that claims the key, `""` meaning the index itself, and null meaning nothing claims it.

routing.why: a root claims every key beneath it
an exact hit on a declared root is a hit, not a miss
THE case this section exists for: roots may nest, and the LONGEST prefix wins
the deeper root does not shadow the shallower one for keys outside its branch
the live estate shape after ticket 30 — not a contrived nesting
routing is segment-wise, never character-wise; `beam.realms` is not under `beam.realm` however much the strings suggest it
a root DEEPER than the key claims nothing; the prefix relation only runs one way
nothing claims it — and the index's own zero-segment root must NOT be the fallback, or no key could ever fail to route and every miss would hand back a registry

null KEY means the zero-segment root key, and it is spelled that way because the empty STRING cannot express it: `routeTo("")` throws, since an empty string arriving from config or a request is a bug rather than an address. So the index's own root is an exact hit — the one way it is reachable — but only through the explicit root constructor. A port that routes by rendered key cannot express this case at all, which is the sharp form of the rule that a wire format must not read `""` as absent.
an exact hit beats the shallower root that also prefixes it
